summary: Current bounded review: receipt-linked provider economics, optional public accounting context, and responsive disclosure behavior. The 24 cases below group 35 automated tests and 12 observed browser procedures; they are not 59 independent automated tests.
Historical reviews remain in the source package. This revision does not claim to have repeated every prior device or browser procedure.
method: Automated: 35 Node calculation/source tests and TypeScript type checking. Browser: direct cloud-Chrome mouse, keyboard, form, clipboard and navigation actions.

Responsive review used a temporary same-origin iframe at 320, 390 and 1280 pixels, with 100% or 200% root-font scaling. Browser scrollbars reduce content widths by 15px. The harness is retained in review notes but is not deployed as a public route.

Screenshots are actual browser captures. The font-scaling harness caused a development hydration warning when it set the root style before React hydration; it is test-only and is absent from the delivered site. Browser-extension metadata errors were also seen and are separate from application behavior.
Public benchmark values were checked against Anthropic S-1/A filed 2026-11-02, Results of Operations p.150 and supplemental expenses p.F-40. Ratios are our calculations, never OpenAI cost estimates.
changes: Primary economics now follows the receipt’s settled bill and explicitly excludes donations.
Dollar-denominated serving costs replace undefined units in the primary view; results distinguish available funds from net profit.
Cost assumptions, loyalty, public benchmarks, formulas and the original five-plan comparison are progressively disclosed.
Economics v3 links restore the receipt and assumptions; reset retains the bill. Legacy comparisons migrate visibly.
Narrow and enlarged text reflows; benchmark numbers no longer split and disclosure symbols no longer overflow.
Readable and machine-readable notes include provenance, definitions, assumptions and exclusions.

cases.title: Default provider ledger
cases.action: Calculate the default bill and illustrative costs.
cases.expected: 100 revenue minus 50 serving, 5 other and 3 payment = 42; serving ceiling 92.
cases.actual: Exact cents assertions pass; no retention improvement is assumed.

cases.title: Receipt boundaries and donation exclusion
cases.action: Evaluate receipt thresholds, large usage and donation variants.
cases.expected: Provider revenue always equals bill(usage).adjusted and excludes gift.
cases.actual: M=585.25 gives revenue 600 and default remainder 527; donation cannot alter revenue.

cases.title: Losses and fee rounding
cases.action: Evaluate excess costs, zero fees and a fractional fee rate.
cases.expected: Preserve losses and cent rounding.
cases.actual: 2.875% of 100 gives 2.88; negative remainders and cost ceilings remain visible.

cases.title: Loyalty and retention math
cases.action: Evaluate 0% and 100% departures, a 20% relative reduction, and oversized discounts.
cases.expected: Finite 12-month horizon; relative percent differs from percentage points; no negative price.
cases.actual: 5% departures reduced by 20% becomes 4%; discount is capped at the settled bill; zero-churn baseline is 454 after acquisition.

cases.title: Shared receipt and assumptions
cases.action: Round-trip v3 economics link with usage 585.25, donation 7.23 and nondefault costs.
cases.expected: Restore numerical assumptions and the associated receipt.
cases.actual: Allowlisted fields and receipt restore exactly.

cases.title: Legacy scenario migration
cases.action: Parse v1/v2 economics links.
cases.expected: Retain advanced inputs, derive metered dollars and explain the change.
cases.actual: Demand 200, base allowance 10 and price 2 become usage 380; warning is provided.

cases.title: Reported figures and calculated ratios
cases.action: Reconcile the cited benchmark and inspect provider defaults.
cases.expected: Expense categories sum to 34,502 million; ratios use 33,242 million revenue; no default is sourced from peer ratios.
cases.actual: Four category ratios round to 14.48, 57.88, 19.91 and 11.52 per 100; serving default remains the independent assumption 50.

cases.title: Existing calculation and source regressions
cases.action: Run all existing model and source tests with the seven new provider tests.
cases.expected: Existing receipt, settlement, source partitions and scenario checks still pass.
cases.actual: All 35 Node tests pass: 28 existing and 7 new. Raw output is included.

cases.title: Type checking
cases.action: Run node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit.
cases.expected: No TypeScript errors.
cases.actual: Passed.

cases.title: Cost input, keyboard and pointer slider
cases.action: Type 120.25, press ArrowRight on the cost slider, then drag the slider with the mouse.
cases.expected: The same input and visible ledger update after each action.
cases.actual: 120.25 produced a -28.25 shortfall; ArrowRight changed it to 120.26 and -28.26; pointer drag later set 134.05 and showed -42.05.

cases.title: Receipt to economics continuity
cases.action: Enter usage 585.25 and custom donation 7.23, then follow the receipt economics link.
cases.expected: Subtotal 605.25 settles to 600; donation produces 607.23 final; provider revenue remains 600.
cases.actual: Observed all values, including payment fee 18 and default remainder 527.

cases.title: Scenario copy and reload
cases.action: Set serving cost 173.48 on that larger bill, copy its link and reload.
cases.expected: The copied URL includes receipt plus costs; reload restores them.
cases.actual: Clipboard contained v3, use=585.25, gift=7.23 and servingCost=173.48. Reload showed bill 600 and remainder 403.52.

cases.title: Reset costs while preserving the bill
cases.action: Reset assumptions after the nondefault shared scenario.
cases.expected: Return cost assumptions to examples, retain current receipt.
cases.actual: Bill stayed 600; serving cost returned to 50 and remainder to 527. Receipt reset separately restored the 100 example.

cases.title: Loyalty relative reduction and benefit cap
cases.action: Set reduction in departures to 20 and a 700 discount on a 600 bill.
cases.expected: 95 of 100 retained without benefit versus 96 with it; discount cannot exceed 600.
cases.actual: Correct retention numbers and a visible 600 cap appeared; negative loyalty result remained visible.

cases.title: Legacy link and advanced isolation
cases.action: Open v2 demand=200, baseUnits=10, rate=2; expand advanced comparison and change demand to 300.
cases.expected: Migration is visible; advanced changes do not rewrite primary receipt.
cases.actual: Original comparison inputs and warning appeared. Primary revenue stayed 500 while advanced settlement revenue changed to 600.

cases.title: History navigation
cases.action: Navigate from economics to Edit the bill, then use browser Back.
cases.expected: Return to economics with assumptions retained.
cases.actual: Returned to v3 demand 300 / rate 2 / receipt usage 380, with comparison revenue 600.

cases.title: Mobile receipt donation sequence
cases.action: At 390px iframe width and 100% text, select the 5 donation.
cases.expected: Donation is below the bill, is explicitly labeled, and updates final total without changing usage.
cases.actual: 100 settled plus 5 donation gave 105 final. Separate custom amount control and commercial-contribution qualification remained readable. No page overflow: 375px client and scroll width.

cases.title: Narrow provider view and enlarged text
cases.action: Inspect 390px default text and 320px at 200% root text; enter serving cost 62.48.
cases.expected: Controls remain editable, values stay visible and content reflows.
cases.actual: Remainder became 29.52; at 320px/200%, client and scroll widths were both 305px. Screenshot retained.

cases.title: Expanded benchmark at 200% narrow text
cases.action: Open benchmark at 320px and 200% text, inspect and repair overflow.
cases.expected: Readable amounts with no page-wide horizontal scroll.
cases.actual: Found a rotating disclosure symbol overflow and split monetary values. Fixed symbol sizing and stacked benchmark rows. Retest: 305px client and scroll widths; amounts such as 57.88 stay intact.

cases.title: Enlarged desktop reflow
cases.action: Inspect provider view at 1280px iframe width and 200% root text.
cases.expected: Columns reflow rather than clipping.
cases.actual: Single-column provider layout remained usable; client and scroll widths both 1265px. Screenshot retained.

cases.title: Direct benchmark entry
cases.action: Navigate directly to #public-benchmarks.
cases.expected: Select economics and open the correct drawer.
cases.actual: Economics selected, benchmark expanded and source link present.

cases.title: Physical mobile touch and Safari
cases.action: Test on physical iPhone/Android browsers.
cases.expected: Native touch dragging, virtual keyboard and browser chrome behave correctly.
cases.actual: Not performed. Cloud Chrome responsive screenshots are not physical-device tests.

cases.title: Assistive technology
cases.action: Use VoiceOver or NVDA through receipt and cost disclosures.
cases.expected: Controls, value changes and navigation are understandable.
cases.actual: Not performed. Accessible labels and actual keyboard actions were inspected, but this is not screen-reader certification.

cases.title: Native browser zoom and OS text settings
cases.action: Test actual browser zoom and mobile OS text enlargement.
cases.expected: Reader settings preserve usability.
cases.actual: Not performed. This pass used responsive iframe widths and 200% root-font scaling, explicitly labeled as simulations.
